title: Declare the canonical URL in the preview URL property
statement: The Open Graph url property carries the same absolute canonical URL the page declares in its canonical link, so a share of any alias resolves to one address.
rationale: Preview caches are keyed by the address they were given, so a page shared through several aliases accumulates separate cached previews and separate share counts for what is one page.
implementation: Read the value from the same builder that produces the canonical link rather than from the incoming request address, so the two cannot diverge and neither reflects a tracking parameter.

verification.method: Extract the Open Graph url property and the canonical link from the same response and confirm both are absolute and identical.

title: Keep preview titles and descriptions truthful to the page
statement: The title and description supplied for a preview describe the content of the page they belong to, and neither promises something the page does not deliver nor is padded with terms for reach.
rationale: The preview is what a reader sees before deciding to open the page, so a preview describing a different or better page converts a share into a disappointment the site chose to cause.
implementation: Default both values to the page title and meta description, and override only where a share context genuinely needs different wording. Do not append the brand or a keyword list to every value in the layout.

verification.method: Compare the preview title and description against the page heading and visible summary for each sampled route.

caution: Each platform truncates preview text at its own point and none publishes a stable limit, so this control governs truthfulness and does not prescribe a character count.

sources.title: The Open Graph protocol, basic metadata

title: Supply alternative text for the preview image
statement: Every declared preview image is accompanied by an alternative text property describing what the image shows.
rationale: Platforms that render the preview to readers using assistive technology have no other description of the image, so omitting it makes the preview inaccessible at the point of sharing rather than on the page.
implementation: Store the description alongside the image on the content record and emit both together, so an image without a description cannot be selected as the preview. For a generated preview image, describe what the generator draws.

verification.method: Report every response declaring a preview image without an accompanying alternative text property.

sources.title: The Open Graph protocol, structured properties

title: Keep preview images fetchable without authentication
statement: The declared preview image returns a successful response to an anonymous request over the production origin, with no session requirement, no crawl directive blocking it, and no hotlink protection rejecting an unknown referrer.
rationale: The platform fetches the image once from outside any session, so an asset that only resolves for a signed-in reader yields a preview with no image and no error the site ever sees.
implementation: Serve preview assets from a path that requires no session and is excluded from referrer-based blocking. Where a firewall challenges unknown clients, allow the asset path rather than weakening the rule for the whole site.

verification.method: Request each declared preview image with no cookies and no referrer and record the status code and content type.

sources.title: The Open Graph protocol, image properties

title: Declare a preview type that matches the page content
statement: The Open Graph type property names the kind of thing the page presents, and any type-specific properties it implies are supplied rather than left to a default.
rationale: The type determines which properties a platform reads and how it lays the preview out, so a page declaring a type it does not satisfy is rendered with fields the site never filled.
implementation: Set the type per route template from what that template renders, rather than declaring one value site-wide in the layout. Where the specification defines no suitable type, use the general one instead of borrowing a closer-sounding mismatch.

verification.method: Record the declared type per route template and compare it against the content the template renders and the properties it emits.

sources.title: The Open Graph protocol, object types

title: Avoid emitting duplicate or conflicting preview properties
statement: Each preview property appears once per response, except where the specification defines the property as repeatable, and a layout default does not survive alongside a page-level override of the same property.
rationale: When one property appears twice, which value a platform reads is its own decision, so the site can supply the right value and still show the wrong preview.
implementation: Merge the layout defaults and the page values in one place before rendering, keying by property name so an override replaces rather than joins the default. Remove any plugin emitting a second copy instead of leaving both.

verification.method: Count occurrences of each preview property in the served response and report any non-repeatable property appearing more than once.

sources.title: The Open Graph protocol, structured properties and arrays

title: Escape user-supplied text before it reaches preview metadata
statement: Any value derived from user input that ends up in a preview property is escaped for the attribute context it is written into, so the input cannot close the attribute, close the tag, or introduce further metadata.
rationale: Preview properties are attribute values in the document head, so unescaped input there can add or replace metadata for the whole page, which turns a comment field into control over how the page is presented elsewhere.
implementation: Write the values through the framework's attribute-escaping path rather than by string concatenation into the template, and strip line breaks and angle brackets from the value before it is used. Treat any content an unauthenticated party can influence as user input.

verification.method: Submit input containing quote, angle bracket, and newline characters through each field that can reach a preview property and inspect the resulting document head.

caution: The cited guidance covers output encoding generally rather than preview metadata specifically, so this record is tier B. The underlying mechanism is ordinary attribute injection and is not in dispute.
